questions.knowledge_point: Multiplying a Matrix by the Identity Matrix
questions.problem:
Calculate the product $J{I}_{2}$ given that ${I}_{2}$ is the $2\times 2$ identity matrix and
$J=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Any matrix, when multiplied by an identity matrix, remains unchanged (assuming that the multiplication is well defined).

The matrix $J$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix and ${I}_{2}$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix too. 

Therefore, the multiplication is well defined and 

$$
J\cdot {I}_{2}=J=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Multiplying a Matrix by a Column or Row of the Identity Matrix
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $B$ is the $3$rd *column* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3}.$

Since we're multiplying the $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ by the $3$rd *column* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3}$, the result must be the $3$rd column of $A.$ Therefore,

$$
AB=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3.5 \\ -4\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Let's check the long way:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & -5 & 5 \\ -5 & 3\sqrt{2} & -3.5 \\ 1 & 2 & -4\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}\cdot 0+(-5)\cdot 0+5\cdot 1 \\ (-5)\cdot 0+3\sqrt{2}\cdot 0+(-3.5)\cdot 1 \\ 1\cdot 0+2\cdot 0+(-4\sqrt{5})\cdot 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3.5 \\ -4\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Since we're multiplying the $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ by the $2$nd *column* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3},$ the result must be the $2$nd *column* of $A.$ Therefore,

$$
AB=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ \sqrt{5} \\ -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Let's check the long way:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & -5 & 2 \\ 3 & \sqrt{5} & -6 \\ 7 & -8 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5}\cdot 0+(-5)\cdot 1+2\cdot 0 \\ 3\cdot 0+\sqrt{5}\cdot 1+(-6)\cdot 0 \\ 7\cdot 0+(-8)\cdot 1+0\cdot 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ \sqrt{5} \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $B$ is the $2$nd *column* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3}.$

Since we're multiplying the $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ by the $2$nd *column* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3},$ the result must be the $2$nd *column* of $A.$ Therefore,

$$
AB=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Let's check the long way:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & 0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot 0+(\frac{-\sqrt{2}}{2})\cdot 1+0\cdot 0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot 0+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot 1+0\cdot 0 \\ 0\cdot 0+0\cdot 1+1\cdot 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $A$ is the $2$nd *row* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3}.$

Since we're multiplying the $3\times 3$ matrix $B$ by the $2$nd *row* of the identity matrix ${I}_{3}$ on the *left*, the result must be the $2$nd *row* of $B.$ Therefore,

$$
AB=[\begin{aligned}-3.5 & -2\sqrt{3} & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Let's check the long way:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4\sqrt{2} & 1.5 & 2 \\ -3.5 & -2\sqrt{3} & -3 \\ 1 & 4 & -\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3.5 & -2\sqrt{3} & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
